newsitem.title: GERMANY: Global One wins Israel phone licence.
newsitem.headline: Global One wins Israel phone licence.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG, the German phone giant, said on Wednesday that its Global One venture with France Telecom and Sprint Corp was part of a consortium that won a licence to operate an international public phone network in Israel.
The consortium, called Barak I.T.C., includes Israeli firms Clalcam Ltd and Matav and marks the first time that Global One's owners bidded jointly on a contract.
"This involvement is an important step in the expansion of the Global One network," Ron Sommer, management board chairman of Deutsche Telekom, said in a statement.
Global One holds 46 percent of the Barak consortium. This is divided up between Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom, each with 10.5 percent, and Sprint, 25 percent.
Clalcom, a leading Israeli provider of value-added telecommunications services, holds 44 percent in the venture and Matav, Israel's second-largest cable television operator, holds 10 percent.
The licence was awarded by the Israeli ministry of telecommunications.
The consortium will offer the full range of Global One services for business and residential customers and other carriers.
The licence is for 10 years and Barak will begin offering services within the next six months.
